patch_description: The current program uses a single Dijkstra shortest path per destination, repeated for all partitions. This can be suboptimal when another destination's cheapest path is slightly more expensive but avoids a shared trunk that the first path already saturates, or when parallel paths allow cheaper per-partition routing. I propose enumerating a bounded set of k-shortest simple paths (k=4) per destination using a generator (never materializing all paths), then greedily assigning each partition to the cheapest candidate path under a congestion penalty that accumulates as partitions are assigned. This reduces redundant transfers by spreading partitions across parallel paths, balances load across networks, and exploits multi-network topologies to minimize total cost, while staying within the Gen 9 safety bound (4-8 candidates preserves 100% success).
